source_doc: Kenneth W. Condit, The Joint Chiefs of Staff and National Policy, vol. II, 1947-1949 (Office of Joint History, 1996), p. 158, citing JCS 1974, 13 Dec 48 and Dec On 23 Dec 48, CCS 373.11 (12-14-48) sec 1 (TROJAN atomic annex)
quote: Twenty of these cities, including Moscow and Leningrad, were considered first priority targets. ... 133 atomic weapons, of which eight would be dropped on Moscow and seven on Leningrad.
notes: Secondary (official history). Only 2 of the 70 TROJAN cities are named; the atomic annex is not online. The Harmon report's city annex (Annex A to App. A, JCS 1953/1, pp38-40) is missing from the NSA copy.
